chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub al-Aqarqufi from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom the dowry of his wife is entrusted, and he reduces it from the dowry of his wives. He said: 'It is added to the dowry of his wives.' And this narration does not contradict the first one, because it is understood that when the dowry is entrusted to him on the condition that he makes it equal to the dowry of his wives, and he falls short of it, then it is added to it. But as for when the matter is entrusted to him absolutely, the ruling is according to what the first report contained, that whatever he rules is valid.

key_terms.يُلْحَقُ: It is added/attached (referring to the shortfall)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband is entrusted with his wife's dowry and reduces it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Basir, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between conditional and absolute entrustment (wakalah) regarding the wife's dowry (mahr). If the mandate was specific to maintaining the full amount, any reduction is rectified by adding the shortfall back; however, if the authority was granted absolutely, the man's discretionary judgment stands as valid and binding. This ruling highlights the nuanced application of agency in Shia jurisprudence, balancing the protection of the wife's financial rights with the autonomy of the appointed trustee.
